notes: Protocol: each case runs twice — once with the skill loaded, once without — and both outputs are graded against the same assertions. The skill earns its keep only if it beats the baseline on its own assertions. Assertions test structure and discipline, never specific values: live data drifts, and several of this skill's load-bearing facts are dated negatives that a single event will flip (a B20 dividend firing, a strip venue launching, an index product shipping) — so assertions demand a dated check or a named evidence tier, not a frozen answer. Understand-mode cases are additionally graded on accessibility: a plain-language anchor before jargon, depth layered on request rather than front-loaded. Grading is judgment, not a script: a model or human reads both outputs and marks each assertion pass or fail; archive a full real graded run as a dated sample output next to this file, with a post-run verification note resolving anything the run flagged as unverified. New capabilities gate on a new case before they land.

Pulls NVDAc from the token-price route (GeckoTerminal). Computes the cross-issuer basis between the two NVDA claim stacks, stamps both legs with their own timestamps, and names the session state. Notes the float/depth asymmetry between the two stacks before calling any spread a mispricing. Closes dated, research-not-advice.

evals.name: build-surface-dev
evals.prompt: I'm a developer. What can I actually build on Base tokenized stocks — what frameworks, tools, and schemes does Base provide, and what's still missing?
evals.expected_output: Maps the build surface in three layers from build-surface.md: rails (the B20 standard with its multiplier and policy-scope reads, the onchain registry, the custody chain, the data rails — with docs.base.org named as the documentation home), integration points (Aerodrome pools, Beefy vaults, the launchpads with their hook-permission read), and whitespace (the dated negatives — no strip venue, no lending market, no index product, the B20-without-a-pool set derived from the registry per session — each named with the rail it would sit on). Names rails and venues by address, not ticker; dates every negative; derives the token, pool, and vault counts from live enumeration (rule 9) instead of quoting a snapshot; distinguishes a tagline from a live venue; states what any build inherits (weekend gap, terms-only dividend, eligibility gating, issuer risk). Read-only: maps the surface, never scaffolds or deploys.
assertions: Maps the three layers — rails, integration points, whitespace — rather than answering as a position question (no price, no yield)
Names the B20 standard's contract-level reads (multiplier, policy scopes) and the registry and custody chain, with docs.base.org as the documentation home
Names rails and venues by contract address (or the address source), never by ticker alone
Dates every negative (no strip venue, no lending market, no index product, the B20-without-a-pool set derived per session rather than a hardcoded count) and names the rail each would sit on
Distinguishes a tagline from a live venue (ecosystem partner pages vs verified contracts) rather than repeating announced support as live
States what a build inherits (weekend gap, terms-only dividend, eligibility gating, issuer risk) and stays read-only — no scaffolding, no deploy
